author: Dee Jefferson
description:
Coups de théâtre abound in the $915m addition to western Sydney’s skyline, which opens on Saturday with five new exhibitions – and a 23-day festival

  • Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email

Dubbed the “Opera House of western Sydney”, Powerhouse Parramatta’s white lattice exoskeleton, composed from 1,300 individual pieces and wrapping 30,000 sq metres of interior space, has already become a familiar landmark.

Even better known, perhaps, is the project’s controversial history. Since the Parramatta outpost was announced in 2014, a vocal group of dissenters led by former staff and trustees has lamented what they see as the neglect of the museum’s Ultimo sit
title: Powerhouse Parramatta opens this weekend – and it’s dazzling inside and out

author: Johana Bhuiyan and agencies
description:
Law bans social media platforms from providing minors features such as autoplay that lead to compulsive use

Google, Meta and TikTok sued California to block enforcement of ⁠a new state law intended ⁠to limit the risk ​of addicting children under 16 to social media platforms.

The law, known as Assembly Bill 1709, prohibits such platforms from offering underage children “psychologically exploitative features” that could lead to compulsive use, such as providing ⁠personal recommendations and sending videos through autoplay features. It also requires the deletion of children’s accounts with those features.

Continue reading...
title: Google, Meta and TikTok sue California to block law protecting children from addiction risk

author: Dani Anguiano and Uwa Ede-Osifo in Los Angeles
description:
Major shake-up as LA councilmember, once considered long shot, ousts Democratic rival she had once endorsed

Nithya Raman was elected to serve as the mayor of Los Angeles, defeating incumbent Karen Bass in a major political shake-up that reflects the growing dissatisfaction with the direction of the city.

The progressive urban planner had served on LA’s city council since 2020. She caused a stir when she entered the race earlier this year hours before the filing deadline – and shortly after endorsing Bass for re-election – and her campaign was once viewed as a long shot.

Continue reading...
title: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman wins Los Angeles mayoral race over incumbent Karen Bass

author: Emine Sinmaz and Geraldine McKelvie
description:
Brand is under investigation over two more rape allegations and police say others could speak up after guilty verdicts

The lead detective in the case against Russell Brand has urged other potential victims of the comedian to come forward after it emerged he is under investigation for two further rape allegations and faces a civil claim in the UK.

Det Supt Andy Furphy, the Metropolitan police’s strategic lead in the investigation, described Brand, 51, as “a predator” whose behaviour escalated as his fame grew.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Our work’s not done’: Russell Brand detective urges other potential victims to come forward

author: Anna Bawden Health and social affairs correspondent
description:
While NHS is identifying more cases, it is failing to meet timescale targets on diagnosis and treatment, experts say

Cancer diagnoses in England have hit record highs of more than 1,000 people a day, NHS figures show.

But experts warned that although the health service was identifying more cases, it was still failing to meet timescale targets on diagnosis and treatment.

Continue reading...
title: Cancer diagnoses in England hit record high of more than 1,000 people a day

author: Sam Levine
description:
Dhillon is first high-level justice department official to leave after historic Republican defeat in 2026 midterms

  • US midterms 2026 live – latest updates

Harmeet Dhillon, a Donald Trump ally who led the justice department’s civil rights division, is leaving her position.

“Today, I accepted the resignation of Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon, who led the Civil Rights Division with conviction the past 18 months. She has defended the civil liberties of every American and enforced the law without fear or favor. The Department is grateful for her dedicated public service, and we wish her every success in her future endeavors,” the attorney general, Todd Blanche, said in a post on X.
title: Harmeet Dhillon, controversial head of DoJ’s civil rights division, steps down

author: Maya Yang and agency
description:
National Weather Service issues flood warning: ‘Seek higher ground now!’

Severe storms brought heavy rain and flash flooding to communities across the Georgia-Tennessee border area late on Wednesday and into Thursday morning that forced dozens of rescues, despite the hazardous conditions making evacuations and efforts to save people difficult.

McCaysville, in north central Georgia, was deluged with up to five inches (13cm) of rain by Thursday morning, triggering life-threatening flash flooding, the National Weather Service (NWS) said. The town lies just across the Toccoa River from Copperhill, Tennessee.

Continue reading...
title: Heavy rains bring flash flooding to Georgia-Tennessee border area

author: Graeme Wearden
description:
Share index slumps 5% amid signs AI industry will face tougher regulation after Democrats’ midterm elections success

The tech-heavy US Nasdaq share index is on track for its worst day in 18 months after slumping by up to 5% on Thursday amid growing signs that the artificial intelligence industry will face tougher regulation after this week’s midterm elections.

As Wall Street sustained widespread losses, the Nasdaq composite tumbled into ‘correction territory’ – more than 10% below its recent record high. The index was heading for its biggest one-day fall since Donald Trump announced his ‘liberation day’ tariffs on US trading partners in April 2025.

Continue reading...
title: Nasdaq heading for worst day in 18 months as Wall Street sustains widespread losses

author: Sam Levin
description:
Measure in blue state requires female athletes prove their sex, which critics warn could lead to ‘invasive’ genital exams

Voters in Washington state have passed a ballot measure banning transgender girls from playing on girls’ sports teams, a major loss for LGBTQ+ rights in a solidly Democratic state.

The measure says students in elementary, middle and high school who want to join girls’ athletics must first submit statements from their healthcare providers verifying their “biological sex”. Opponents have raised alarms the measure may force girls to endure “invasive and extreme” genital exams to participate in school sports.

Continue reading...
title: Washington state passes ballot measure banning trans girls from school sports

author: Anna Betts
description:
Black in defamation lawsuit alleges California lawmaker made false statements about his ties to Jeffrey Epstein

Billionaire Leon Black has filed a defamation lawsuit against California congressman Robert Garcia, accusing the lawmaker, who is the top Democrat on the House oversight committee, of making false statements about his ties to Jeffrey Epstein and the disgraced financiers’s sex trafficking crimes.

The filing, filed in federal court in New York on Wednesday, comes almost two months after the House voted to hold Black in contempt of Congress over his refusal to comply with subpoenas issued by the House oversight committee as part of the panel’s investigation into Epstein. As of 5 November, the Department of Justice has not filed contempt charges against Black. Garcia’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
title: Leon Black sues US congressman Robert Garcia for $7.5m over Epstein comments

author: Ariana Baio in Washington
description:
JD Vance, Ron DeSantis and Ted Cruz all pointed to Iran war and affordability as key factors in Democratic victory

  • US midterms 2026 live – latest updates

Republican hopefuls in the race to succeed Donald Trump swiftly blamed two key pillars of his agenda – the Iran war and tariffs – for summoning the Democratic blue wave that swept the US midterm elections.

JD Vance, the outgoing Florida governor Ron DeSantis and the senator Ted Cruz
title: Republicans hoping to succeed Trump in 2028 dissect midterm rout

author: Michael Savage Media editor
description:
Concerns remain that media industry is still failing to confront troubling behaviour

Even within the culture of casual misogyny and sexism that pervaded the TV world in the mid-noughties, Naomi Harvey and her colleagues concluded they needed to do something about Russell Brand.

Harvey was one of a team of researchers tasked with finding fans of Big Brother, Channel 4’s reality TV juggernaut, to appear on the discussion show Big Brother’s Big Mouth, hosted by Brand.

Continue reading...
title: Misogyny and sexism of Russell Brand case have not gone away, say TV insiders

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Telecoms group reports £1.1bn pre-tax profit in six months to end of September and share price touches five-year high

  • Business live – latest updates

BT has cut almost 8,000 jobs since the end of March as it pushes ahead with sweeping cost reductions across the business.

The telecoms group said its workforce had fallen by 7,731 to 90,000, excluding staff in its international business, which is being spun out in a joint venture with the US telecoms company Verizon. It had a workforce of about 130,000 people, including contractors, two years ago.

Continue re
title: BT cuts almost 8,000 jobs amid sweeping cost-saving programme

author: Michael Sainato
description:
New policy would permit passengers to take firearms to their seats in lockboxes on 1,500 trains a day across the US

The Transport Workers Union, which represents 360 onboard service workers at national passenger rail operator Amtrak, has lambasted the planned implementation of a new policy that would permit passengers to bring their guns on its US intercity trains.

The forthcoming protocols will allow people to carry on firearms in personal lock boxes.

Continue reading...
title: Amtrak workers’ union denounces plan to let passengers bring guns on trains: ‘Sheer lunacy’

author: Carl Smith
description:
The BLVD is home to 250 enterprises, from banks, tattoo shops and restaurants to museums and a performing arts centre

Passing through the Mojave desert on State Route 14, going by landscapes Hollywood uses to represent alien planets, a driver might not expect to find a walkable, tree-lined boulevard.

But there are nine beautiful, leafy blocks on West Lancaster Boulevard, a piece of what used to be Highway 14. They were redeveloped as part of a mixed-use urban streetscape in the city of Lancaster, California in 2010.

The BLVD, as it’s been rebranded, is home to 250 public and private enterprises, from banks, tattoo shops and restaurants to museums, a performing arts centre and a public library. City Hall is just a block south.

The city invested $11.5m (£8.5m) to transform a busy thoroughfare into an inviting public space. The three lanes in the centre of the former five-lane road were replaced by a series of tree-lined ramblas –
title: ‘It’s kind of a melting pot’: how one US city transformed a highway into a leafy oasis

author: Josh Butler
description:
Albanese should tread carefully as he struggles to make case for how the new technology will benefit ordinary voters

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

When will Australia see the benefits of the AI and datacentre boom? So far, all we’ve seen is the possibility of changes to copyright which would hurt Australian creatives, special rules about power and water use, and the threat of mass displacement or replacement of workers, with the trade-off being a mere
title: Australians are yet to see the benefits of AI and datacentres – and US midterms show they could be political kryptonite

author: Penry Buckley and Henry Belot
description:
Transparency experts raise concerns about plans to use NDA to gag attendees at event featuring Pauline Hanson in lead-up to NSW election

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation is attempting to gag donors from ever revealing details of discussions at an invite-only, cocktail-dress fundraiser with the party’s senior leadership team, in a move described as a “worrying precedent” for democracy.

Invitations to the “very special evening” at an undisclosed central Sydney venue next Thursday show donors will be charged $3,000 for a “private and very discrete” four-hour event.

Continue reading...
title: One Nation asks donors at $3,000-a-head Sydney fundraiser to accept ‘non-disclosure agreement’

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
Hundreds of first responders worked to control the blaze, and a lithium-ion battery was found at the scene

Six people died in a fire that roared through a residential home in New York City early on Thursday and seven others were injured, including three firefighters, the city’s fire department said.

The major fire was reported in the early hours in Brooklyn and brought more than 200 first responders rushing to attend to the blaze and those trapped by it, in the city borough’s Sunset Park neighborhood.

Continue reading...
title: Six people dead and seven injured after fire at Brooklyn home

author: Phillip Inman
description:
Bank’s decision goes contrary to analysis from Office for Budget Responsibility that predicts lower inflation and little impetus for wage growth

  • Bank of England raises interest rates to 4%

  • Business live – latest updates

An interest rate rise by the Bank of England to 4% is a big call when households are suffering from a second cost of living crisis in four years.

Many people will be incredulous when they hear of the decision to increase the cost of borrowing by 0.25 percentage points, looking around their neighbourhood for s
title: Interest rate rise in midst of cost of living crisis will leave many incredulous

author: Rory Carroll in Dublin, Gwyn Topham in London and Angela Giuffrida in Rome
description:
Planes forced into emergency landings or diversions two days after hoax alerts affected air travel

  • Europe live – latest updates

Bomb threats have caused diversions and emergency landings for at least 15 flights across Europe, renewing questions about a possibly coordinated effort to disrupt travel.

The series of warnings on Thursday morning affected flights between Italy, Ireland, the UK, Spain, Bulgaria, Romania, Poland, Finland, Austria, Denmark, Belgium, Portugal, Greece and Czechia.

Continue reading...<
title: Bomb threats disrupt at least 15 flights across Europe, raising hybrid war fears

author: Martin Belam
description:
Criticism of US-Israel war on Iran seen as huge factor in Democrats’ sweeping victory. Plus, a spiky customer steps into a North Carolina bagel store

Good morning.

Donald Trump has accepted the results of the US midterm elections as the system held up against attempts at election interference. His administration had waged an aggressive effort to sow doubt about the results in advance, but the worst fears have not been realized. “It was essentially too big to rig,” an unnamed Trump adviser told CNN, after Democrats swept into power across the nation on a “blue wave”. Trump made a public appearance the day after the seismic results – chiefly to talk about his new White House ballroom plans.

Follow
title: Trump accepts election results as Republicans face midterm reckoning | First Thing

author: Graeme Wearden
description:
Ten-year high shows sterling’s strength against other currencies following fall of dollar after US midterm elections

  • Business live – latest updates

The pound has hit its highest level since its crash in the wake of the Brexit referendum a decade ago.

Data released by the Bank of England on Thursday showed that the pound reached its strongest level against a basket of other currencies since 23 June 2016 – the day of the EU vote – on Wednesday.

Continue reading...
title: Pound hits highest level since its crash after 2016 Brexit vote

author: Lauren Aratani
description:
Polling done for the Guardian shows plummeting support from a former key constituency of Donald Trump’s base

Polling conducted by the Harris Poll for the Guardian before the election shows just how angry voters were and points to one key reason Republicans lost so badly: plummeting support from rural voters, once a key constituency of Donald Trump’s base.

Over the summer, 95% of Americans indicated they believed there was an affordability crisis, particularly because of steep gas and grocery prices. By October, 61% of voters believed the country was experiencing a recession, even though technically it wasn’t.

Continue reading...
title: Rural voters were feeling left behind before the midterms, poll shows

author: Chris Stein
description:
Democrats gain hundreds of seats in historic victories – and party set to embark on aggressive legislative spree

The blue wave that swept Republicans out of power across the United States didn’t just strike Congress. In Tuesday’s midterm elections, Democrats gained hundreds of seats in state legislatures across the country, under-the-radar victories that may have major implications for life in America.

Though ballots are still being counted, the party’s success appear to be historic – Democrats haven’t won full control of government in Arizona in 60 years, in Pennsylvania since the 1990s, and Wisconsin since their wipeout in 2010. In Michigan and Minnesota, they regained trifectas they lost after the 2024 election, while in Texas, they will control the state house for the first time since 2002.

Continue reading...
title: Not just Congress: Democrats’ blue wave washes over state legislatures across US

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Voters in Nevada, Virginia, Missouri and Idaho passed or strengthened protections for women’s reproductive freedom

Reproductive rights were on the ballot on Tuesday night as voters weighed in on several abortion-related measures, delivering a largely successful night for reproductive rights advocates encompassed by a historic blue wave.

In Nevada, voters approved an amendment enshrining abortion rights in the state constitution, permanently protecting access to abortion through the second trimester after a second referendum on the measure.

Continue reading...
title: Reproductive rights protected in several states by midterm election ballot measures

author: Sandra Laville
description:
With parts of region served by company in severe drought still, regulators give it six weeks to come up with action plan

Repeated failures by South West Water to tackle leaks are putting customers at higher risks of losing water supplies as parts of the region remain in severe drought, regulators have said.

In a warning to the privatised company that serves 1.8 million people across the south-west of England, the regulators said it had been failing to meet targets to reduce leaks and repair burst pipes for seven years.

Continue reading...
title: South West Water’s failure to fix leaks ‘putting customer supplies at risk’

author: Caroline Davies and agency
description:
Tej Singh Bhandal, 68, was pulled from a queue and detained under terrorism law in ‘creeping criminalisation of protest action’

The Metropolitan police have settled a claim brought by a 68-year-old pro-Palestinian activist who accused the force of treating him “like a criminal” when he was arrested under anti-terrorism legislation.

Tej Singh Bhandal was returning to the UK on Eurostar earlier this year when he was pulled from a queue by police at St Pancras International, London.

Continue reading...
title: Met settles claim brought by Palestine activist ‘treated like a criminal’ during arrest

author: Sam Levine
description:
Administration had waged aggressive bid to sow doubt about midterms results but worst fears were not realized

In the months leading up to the midterm elections, Donald Trump’s administration waged an aggressive effort to sow doubt about the results, intimidate voters and election officials, and signal they would use the power of the federal government to challenge the electoral process.

But when the results came in Tuesday night, revealing a massive blowout for the GOP, Trump did something almost unprecedented: he accepted the results. Trump said he was “absolutely willing” to accept the outcome and looked forward to working with Democrats. With the exception of the 2024 election, which he won and Republicans performed well in, Trump has raised doubt about every presidential race and midterm since his first election in 2016.
title: Trump accepts midterm results as system holds up against election interference efforts

author: Press Association
description:
Gordon Brothers still in ‘active discussions’ with interested parties and seeking to ‘protect as many jobs as possible’

The US owner of Poundland has said the high street chain remains “challenged and vulnerable” after holding talks with ministers amid government criticism of its handling of the retailer.

Gordon Brothers said in a statement on Thursday morning that it was still in “active discussions” with interested suitors and had been seeking to “protect as many jobs as possible”.

Continue reading...
title: Poundland’s US owner says retailer remains ‘vulnerable’, after talks with ministers

author: Danny Vincent in Hong Kong
description:
Wong, 30, in prison since 2020, is only activist in Hong Kong prosecuted twice under national security law

  • Exclusive: Joshua Wong laments city’s fate from inside maximum security prison

The Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong has been sentenced to 10 years in prison after earlier pleading guilty to “foreign collusion”, his second conviction under a national security law critics say has been used to silence political opposition in the city.

Wong, who rose to prominence as the teenage face of Hong Kong’s 2014 pro-democracy demonstrations,
title: Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in prison in national security case

author: Sarah Basford Canales
description:
One Nation leader granted special leave to appeal after full federal court earlier this year agreed Hanson portrayed Faruqi as a ‘second-class citizen’

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s high court has agreed to hear Pauline Hanson’s appeal against a ruling that she engaged in racial discrimination against Mehreen Faruqi when she told the Greens senator to “pack your bags and piss off back to Pakistan”.

The One Nation leader was granted special leave to appeal on Thursday after the full federal court earlier this year unanimously upheld a 2024 decisi
title: ‘Bring it on’: Pauline Hanson to appeal Mehreen Faruqi racial discrimination ruling in high court

author: Sian Cain
description:
Court finds ‘clear and numerous similarities’ between two medical dramas, allowing lawsuit by ER creator’s widow Sherri to go to jury trial in 2027

The Pitt is similar enough to ER to allow Michael Crichton’s widow to pursue a long-running lawsuit over the award-winning medical drama, a US appeals court has ruled.

In a unanimous opinion filed on Wednesday, a three-judge panel denied an appeal from Warner Bros Television (WBTV), which has argued for two years that the shows are unrelated.

Continue reading...
title: The Pitt and ER are similar enough for Michael Crichton’s widow’s lawsuit to proceed, court rules

author: Kat Wong
description:
The 31-year-old former police officer is accused of fatally shooting couple Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Sydney in 2024

  • Former police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon enters witness box in Sydney double murder trial

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Lamarre-Condon describes relationship to Jesse Baird

The police officer is responding to questions about the beginning of their relationship:

For the months of October and November 2022 it was friends with a sexual relationship. When we would meet up it was of the sexual nature. By December 2022 that’s when we began going on ro
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon trial live updates: accused double murderer gives evidence in high-profile case

author: Nick Robins-Early
description:
The tech billionaire set spending record as he poured $446m into campaigns for failed Republican candidates

Elon Musk set a record for election spending this year after pouring nearly half a billion dollars into backing Republicans in the US midterm elections. It turned out to be a poor investment.

The SpaceX and Tesla CEO contributed at least $446m to Republican-aligned Super Pacs and groups over the course of the elections, specifically targeting several key
title: Elon Musk’s nearly half a billion dollars in midterms spending was a flop

author: Kat Wong and Ima Caldwell
description:
Lamarre-Condon gives evidence in court after pleading not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in early 2024

  • Live updates: Beau Lamarre-Condon gives evidence in murder trial

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Former officer Beau Lamarre-Condon has alleged he heard homophobic abuse when working for New South Wales police, as the 31-year-old gave evidence in his double murder trial in Sydney.

Lamarre-Condon is accused of fatally shooting couple Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19
title: Former police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon enters witness box in Sydney double murder trial

author: Johana Bhuiyan
description:
Voters approved nearly every datacenter moratorium that was on the ballot, dozens in total in Tuesday’s elections

  • Track live results from all 50 states

  • Send us your questions about the US midterms results and Democrats’ ‘blue wave’

There were three big losers in Tuesday’s midterm elections in the US: Donald Trump, Elon Musk and datacenters.

Datacenters, the facilities full of semiconductor chips that power artificial intelligence and a host of other online products, were on the ballot in elections in at least 40 jurisdictions across 10 states. Voters responded with a strong rebuke of the giant buildings, which have has become a symbol of the tech industry and AI.
title: Datacenters were on the ballot. US voters rejected them

author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
description:
Exclusive: Government should introduce ‘flexi-jobs’ alongside subsidies and skills support, former minister will say

The British state should create and subsidise paid jobs for thousands of disabled young people as part of an “opportunity revolution” aimed at reversing years of labour market discrimination, the Milburn review of youth employment will recommend.

The review, due to report this month, will say the government should introduce “flexi-jobs” alongside employment subsidies and intensive skills support to make it easier for disabled and chronically ill 16- to 24-year-olds to get work.

Continue reading...
title: Milburn review to call for jobs ’revolution’ for young people with disabilities
